title: A second reader the agent cannot skip: how two wrong emails became a gate on every draft

items.text: On 9 October two emails from agent@riskmandate.ai went out in the author's first person and signed "Dinis"

items.text: A rule kept by the agent it governs is hope
items.anchor: A rule kept by the agent it governs is hope.

items.text: A self-held rule can be forgotten, misread, summarised away, or argued around by the agent's own reasoning
items.anchor: It can be forgotten, misread, summarised away, or argued around by the agent's own reasoning.

items.text: The fix has two parts: a second independent reader, and a gate the harness runs on the tool call so the agent cannot skip it
items.anchor: A second, independent reader, and a gate the drafting agent cannot skip because the harness, not the agent, runs it on the tool call.

items.text: Certain things go in code; signatures, dashes, key shapes, HTML and recipients are checked deterministically before any model
items.anchor: Signatures, dashes, key shapes, HTML and recipients are checked deterministically before any model is called.

items.text: The checker gets less than the author on purpose: no history, no tools, ideally a different model
items.anchor: No conversation history, no tools, ideally a different model: only the rules, the sources and the draft.

items.text: Anything but an explicit PASS is a FAIL; a late email is cheap, a wrong one cannot be taken back
items.anchor: A late email is cheap; a wrong one cannot be taken back.

items.text: The pattern is old: segregation of duties (banks), the two-person rule (military), independent double check (pharmacies)
items.anchor: Banks call it segregation of duties, the military calls it the two-person rule, pharmacies call it an independent double check.

items.text: R1 voice: mail with a To must carry the agent's signature, and none of the three lines before it a sign-off in the author's name; only the visible email is read
items.anchor: R1 voice | For mail with a To: the body must carry the agent's signature line, and none of the three lines before it may be a sign-off in my name. Only the visible email is read, not the thread summary below it.

items.text: R4 dashes: no em or en dashes anywhere

items.text: The reusable pattern in six steps, as the inbox agent wrote them
items.anchor: In six steps, as the inbox agent wrote them:

items.text: Step 1: pick the tool call that matters (Slack message, CRM write, page publish, vault commit, payment API)
items.anchor: **Pick the tool call that matters**: sending a Slack message, writing to the CRM, publishing a page, committing to a vault, a payment API.

items.text: Step 2: write the rules as a short numbered checklist with a fixed answer format
items.anchor: **Write the rules as a short numbered checklist** with a fixed answer format.

items.text: Step 3: put everything certain into code first; leave only judgement to the model
items.anchor: **Put everything certain into code first**; leave only judgement to the model.

items.text: Step 4: give the checker only rules, sources and the proposed action; no history
items.anchor: **Give the checker only what it needs**: rules, sources, the proposed action. No history.

items.text: Step 5: deny on anything other than an explicit PASS
items.anchor: 5. **Deny on anything other than an explicit PASS.**

items.text: Step 6: log every verdict
items.anchor: 6. **Log every verdict.**

items.text: Next candidates in the team: CRM agent writes, newsroom page promotions, Slack posts, the leak check before vault push
items.anchor: The next candidates in our own team are the CRM agent's writes (no keys, no unverified facts presented as verified), the newsroom's page promotions (nothing indexed until I promote it; quotes are claims), Slack posts

items.text: On this site the leak check before a vault push is still a script the author runs, not a gate
items.anchor: the leak check before any vault push, which on this site is still a script I run rather than a gate I cannot skip

items.text: The guard is only as independent as its installation; today it is a setting
items.anchor: It is only as independent as its installation

items.text: R7 is only as good as the sources, and the drafter writes them
items.anchor: R7 is only as good as the sources

items.text: The checker can be wrong in both directions; expect false FAILs, which cost a retry
items.anchor: The checker can be wrong in both directions.

items.text: It checks drafts, not sending; the author sends, and the no-send rule is a separate barrier question
items.anchor: The rule that agents never send is enforced separately, and is a different barrier question.

items.text: It does not replace reading: a PASS means ten rules held, not that the email is good
items.anchor: A PASS means ten rules held, not that the email is good.

items.text: The rule that lived in four paragraphs now lives on the tool call, with a log, one step short of a control
items.anchor: a rule that used to live in four paragraphs now lives on the tool call, with a log, and a clear statement of the one step left before it is a control

flags: In short says 'the military calls it the two-person rule', but the body attributes the two-person rule only to NIST's definition of separation of duty; the military attribution is not supported in the body. Anchor: 'Banks call it segregation of duties, the military calls it the two-person rule, pharmacies call it an independent double check.'

Six kinds of independence: the six kinds are not named individually in the text, and 'Two rows deserve a comment' and 'the last column' refer to a table that exists only inside the image ck-independence.webp, so the scores (none, four, all six) cannot be checked from the article text. Anchor: 'The drafter re-reading its own draft has none; the guard as it runs today has four; the guard under managed settings, with sources written by someone else, has all six.'

Cost estimate not reproducible from the stated figures: the input/output split and days per month are not given; 4.5M to 9M tokens a month gives $9 to $18 if all input, and no single fixed split gives exactly $12 to $21. Anchor: 'At 5,000 to 10,000 tokens a draft and thirty drafts a day, that is roughly $12 to $21 a month'

Superlative without support: 'the oldest control in finance' is asserted but the earliest cited source is the 1998 Basel framework. Anchor: 'What the inbox agent built is maker-checker, the oldest control in finance.'

The checker uses ten numbered rules, but only R1, R3, R4, R5, R6 and R7 are identified; R2 and R8 to R10 are never named, so 'A PASS means ten rules held' cannot be fully traced.
